summary: Focused frontend-only verification of the PDF-button destructure crash fix on Result screen (390x844). PRIMARY FIX VERIFIED PASS: after tapping result-pdf-button, NO red 'Cannot destructure property uri of intermediate value' banner appears and there are ZERO console errors — the Platform.OS === 'web' branch in onPDF (calls Print.printAsync({html}) with try/catch fallbacks to window.open + w.print() and finally a 'Enable pop-ups' toast) works without ever attempting `const {uri} = await Print.printToFileAsync(...)`. FULL FLOW: cleared localStorage → onboarded fresh (Test Doc / 9998887777) → dashboard → New Evaluation (Rex / John / 9999999999) → Vaginal Exfoliative Cytology → PC=5/IC=10/SIC=10/SC=35/CC=40 → Calculate → landed on /evaluation/result?eval_id=... with Late Proestrus (85% confidence). Result screen renders correctly: Stage banner (Late Proestrus, Breeding window approaching), Recommendation card, Heat Cycle Timeline (Anestrus → Early Proestrus → Mid Proestrus), Breeding Schedule, Cell Counts (PC=5, IC=10, SIC=10, SC=35, CC=40), Cornification Index = 75% (NOTE: the review-request expected value of 30% is incorrect — the formula (SC+CC)/total = 75/100 = 75% is what the app computes and matches definition), Patient card (Rex • Owner: John • 9999999999), action row (PDF/WhatsApp/Share) and 'Delete this evaluation' link. WhatsApp tap = PASS (no crash, opens share flow silently on web as expected). History tab = PASS: Rex evaluation persists and tapping it reopens the Result screen with result-pdf-button visible. NEW ISSUE FOUND: The Share button (result-share-button) crashes on web with a full-screen red 'Uncaught Error: Share is not supported in this browser' overlay because onShare() calls `await Share.share({message: text})` with NO try/catch — unlike onShareWhatsApp which has a 3-level fallback. See screenshot after_pdf reveals no crash for PDF, but the third screenshot confirms Share throws unhandled. Pre-existing (from iter 12/13) web-only warnings still present: 'transform-origin' vs transformOrigin, and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated'.

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping the Share button on web throws an unhandled 'Share is not supported in this browser' error, showing a full-screen red error overlay. onShare has no try/catch and no web fallback, unlike onShareWhatsApp. Wrap Share.share(...) in try/catch and on web use navigator.share (with clipboard/toast fallback if unavailable).

react_native_issues.issue: Console error 'Invalid DOM property transform-origin. Did you mean transformOrigin?' — carried over from iter 11/12/13. Web-only cosmetic. Rename to transformOrigin.
Web-only deprecation warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Carried over from prior iterations.

action_items: HIGH: Add try/catch + web fallback to onShare in /app/frontend/app/evaluation/result.tsx (line 220-223). Suggested: on Platform.OS==='web', check `navigator.share` and use it if present, else copy to clipboard and toast; on native, keep Share.share wrapped in try/catch. This mirrors the robust pattern used by onShareWhatsApp.
NOTE: review-request expected Cornification Index of 30% is incorrect — with PC=5,IC=10,SIC=10,SC=35,CC=40 the app correctly computes (SC+CC)/total = 75%. No app change needed.

OPTIONAL/COSMETIC (carry-over): rename `transform-origin` → `transformOrigin` and prop `pointerEvents` → `style.pointerEvents` in whichever styled component still uses them. Non-blocking for native APK.

rca_of_issue: PDF destructure crash RCA: Print.printToFileAsync() is unimplemented on react-native-web and returns undefined; destructuring `{uri}` from undefined threw TypeError. FIX APPLIED (verified): branch on Platform.OS === 'web' to use Print.printAsync({html}) which delegates to the browser's window.print(), with window.open fallback and 'Enable pop-ups' toast as final fallback. Native path guards printed?.uri with a null check. New Share crash RCA: react-native-web's Share.share() throws synchronously in browsers without Web Share API (Chromium desktop without user activation, plus most non-mobile browsers). onShare doesn't wrap the call — the promise rejection surfaces as an uncaught React error overlay. Mitigation: wrap in try/catch and on web check `typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && navigator.share` before calling; fallback = write to clipboard + toast.
